subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global agent dry-run mode, and which tool execution surfaces must be covered before it is safe to present as a no-side-effects boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but automation should not choose the product/security contract for Gateway, embedded, client-hosted, plugin, backend, and native runtime tool paths.

options.title: Define the safety contract first
options.body: Specify supported surfaces, preview/result shape, hook ordering, read-only exemptions, and unsupported paths before implementing the flag.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Keep this issue as the focused tool-preview requirement while coordinating terminology and scope with the broader Ask/Plan/Modify work.

options.title: Decline global dry-run
options.body: Keep command-specific dry-runs and existing tool policy hooks as the supported safety tools, then close this direction after a maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Define the safety contract first
recommendation.body: Specify supported surfaces, preview/result shape, hook ordering, read-only exemptions, and unsupported paths before implementing the flag.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the shared tool adapter and execution-boundary design is Peter Steinberger's prior work in this area.
